Ventilation and noise in a cognitive day care centre: environmental
quality analysis and design optimization study
W. Li1 · Z. Du2,4 · Z. Wu3 · M. Yu3
Received: 11 November 2022 / Revised: 30 January 2023 / Accepted: 22 February 2023 / Published online: 11 March 2023
© The Author(s) under exclusive licence to Iranian Society of Environmentalists (IRSEN) and Science and Research Branch, Islamic Azad University 2023
Abstract
In the context of epidemic normalization, it is particularly important to explore environmental health from the perspective
of adaptation of patient pathological characteristics to achieve sustainable goals. Although recent studies have confirmed
the effects of ventilation and sound on human health and revealed that improvement in the quality of patient recovery can be
achieved by controlling the material exchange between people and the environment, it remains unclear in terms of the mutual
drivers of intangible material (ventilation and sound) and patient recovery quality. This study establishes a link between
the physical environment and the quality of rehabilitation by reporting on the ventilation and noise levels at a rehabilitation
facility for people with cognitive disorders. Second, a successful design optimization technique based on the adaption of
pathological traits is suggested. The Centre fails to fulfil the ventilation and acoustic criteria for indoor comfort, according
to the findings of the real testing. The study procedure demonstrates that (1) enhancing the space's openness to unblock the
airflow can only have its effect maximised if the layout is taken into account to accommodate the wind direction.; (2) the
spatial scale is not the only factor affecting the sound quality of the environment; and (3) increasing the openness of the area
can improve the quality of sound transmission and reduce noise in the area, but at the same time, it will have some impact
on other areas.
Keywords Cognitive disorders · Pathological adaptation · Environmental health · Ventilation · Acoustic environment ·

ventilation and noise in a cognitive care facility are thor-
oughly investigated in this research, and the best design
approaches are also explored. Patients with cognitive dis-
orders are typical of the most prevalent and common types
of geriatric disorders. The body needs more time to adjust
to changes in physical factors such external temperature
and humidity as we age, and older individuals have fewer
environmental adaptations in biological functioning. A
number of theories of environment-assisted rehabilitation
offer a window of opportunity for spatial intervention and
delay, and this research offers an illuminating role for the
spatial practise of rehabilitation for patients with cognitive
problems.
Using the environmental adaptations of the physical
functions of cognitive patients as a basis, this research first
establishes a link between the quality of rehabilitation and
the physical environment. In order to comprehend the pre-
sent situation of the physical environment in contemporary
nursing homes, a thorough empirical investigation of the
ventilation, lighting, and noise environments at the Guang-
zhou Yuexiu Senior Citizen Service Center was carried out.
After simulating the actual ventilation and noise environ-
ment using the CFD green building technology software
from PHOENICS and ECOTECT, the optimal design option
is discovered through model comparison and iteration. The
physical environment design techniques that are helpful for
the rehabilitation of patients with cognitive disorders are
finally summarised, their applicability, generalisation, and
variability in practise are discussed, and practical solution
avenues are suggested for studies of a similar nature.
Materials and methods
Theories and research pathways
Hamilton pointed out that the factors that influence a per-
son's behaviour include both environmental and non-envi-
ronmental factors, and that it is more reasonable to use a
multidisciplinary research approach (Zeisel 2006). To this
end, he constructed the "environment-behavior-neurosci-
ence" trinity of sociological research methods (Table 1).
The general steps of this method of research are: (1) to fully
understand the behaviour of the research subjects through
various methods such as behavioural observation method
and expert consultation; (2) to obtain the health variable
indicators of the patients through instruments and construct
their constitutive links with behavioural characteristics,
physiological characteristics, pathological characteristics,
etc.; (3) to find the mutual influence relationship between
the environment and the rehabilitation of the disease, and
innovatively translate and apply them in the design practice
to create a space beneficial to health.

For individuals with cognitive impairments, boosting
ventilation and minimising noise is an effective method to
enhance the quality of their rehabilitation. Poor ventilation
and excessive noise may impair neurological function and
aggravate cognitive loss (Weuve et al. 2021; Paul et al.
2019). The wind simulation and sound simulation tools
PHOENICS and ECOTECT are well known in the indus-
try. Both programmes provide a broad variety of param-
eter options, strong model compatibility, and precise data
analysis. The fourth level of the service centre, which is
the primary floor for patient activity, will be the site scope
for this paper's in-depth investigation. We will utilise these
two software tools to simulate building performance and
examine optimization strategies.
